provenance lives only in a comment, so a future edit cannot be checked mechanically.","fix":"Note in the header that K and IV are the fractional parts of the cube and square roots of the first primes, so a reviewer can regenerate them."}],"strengths":["All eight interface ports match the spec exactly in name, direction, and width, including the 512-bit big-endian block and 256-bit digest.","Every one of the sixty-four datapath updates happens in S_RUN counted 0 through 63, and S_FINAL performs only the hash addition and the strobe, so the compression cannot run a sixty-fifth round.","done is assigned a default of low each cycle and raised only in S_FINAL, which makes the single-cycle strobe structural rather than a matter of timing.","busy falls in the same cycle done rises, so a back-to-back start on the done cycle is accepted exactly as the spec requires.","The rolling sixteen-word window implements the schedule recurrence directly from its own taps, so W[t] for t below 16 and the recurrence above it share one storage structure without a special case.","init selects between the FIPS initial values and the held digest at the single load point, making multi-block chaining a mux rather than a second datapath.","Reset clears every output the spec names — busy, done and digest — and returns the state machine to idle, abandoning a block in flight.","State is encoded in a plain two-bit register with named localparams, so the encoding is visible at the declaration and no name is declared twice."],"summary":"The module implements all eleven Must requirements: the schedule recurrence, the sixty-four-round working-variable update, the final modular addition into the incoming hash values, the start-only-while-idle rule, the one-cycle done strobe with busy low in that cycle, and the synchronous active-low reset. The round-count structure is the part most likely to be wrong in a design of this kind, and it is right here: sixty-four updates in the running state, commit-only in the finish state. The three issues raised are area and timing observations plus a documentation note; none of them changes behaviour."}
